findings.raw_source: <mi a_>  {n} `a ^word, a few words', e.g. <mi a_reyo_ kari_m>  {`say at least something'; (when followed by a noun)} `a ^mouthful', e.g. <mi a_ jilu> `a mouthful of meat'.  $00016*$

<asul>  {v} `to ^support; to ^provide food for'.  !The forms <asultana> and <asulakana> are both used in the sense `regularly have enough to eat', e.g. <esuko asultana/asulakana>__`they have plenty to eat'.  ??  $00377$
<bondo>  {v} `to ^close (from Hindi, used in certain metaphorical usages, e.g. <paiTi: bondokeDa>__"He closed down the work")'.  $01174$

<boro>  {v} `to ^fear; to be ^afraid.__When the object of the fear is not expressed, this is used transitively, e.g. <borokeDae:>__"He was afraid", <alom boroya (boro-e-a)>__"Don't be afraid".__When the object of fear is expressed it takes a <-te> or <-a> marker, e.g. <alom borotekowa> or <alom borowakowa>__"Do not be afraid of them".__<Boro> is used in an impersonal construction with the experiencer as object, e.g. <eDka borokiDJa>__"I was thoroughly scared".__It is also sometimes used with a personal subject and a direct personal object with the meaning "to make someone give in (give up) out of fright'.  $01232$

<boroncho>  {adv} `^rather (following the preferred person or action, e.g. <am boroncho seno:me>__"rather you go (then someone else)"); <manDi boroncho jomem>__"rather eat food (then drink rice beer)'.  $01247$

<buru>  {n} `a ^mountain, a ^hill, a ^jungle'; {v} `to ^heap_up (used also as verbal affixes with other verbs in this  sense, e.g. <dul-buru>__"to pour in a heap"); poetic parallel with <bonga>, a spirit, to ^sacrifice'; {vr} `poetic parallel with <bonga> or <goe:> having the meaning "to become a ^spirit" (said e.g. in prayers to the ancestors); note the expression <buruken chauli> used in prayers as follows: <buruken chauli gaRaken mayomeJ punjiyama-hinjiyama>__"I put in the <punji> heaped up rice grains for you, I cause rivers of blood to flow for you' (i.e. "I offer you numerous sacrifices").  $01362$

<chada:-chada:>  {v} `to ^jump up and down with both feet together (used esp. of small birds) (often used with <-tan> and verbs such as <sen> or <nir>, e.g. <chada:chada:tane: nireya>__"He will run away hopping along") (also <dacha:-dacha:>)'.  $01461$
